title: Klezmory
program_note:
Klezmory is meant as a memory of the klezmer music performed at a wedding about a century ago, in Eastern Europe.  The main melodic source for this piece is “Khosn Khale Mazel Tov” (Congratulations to the Bride and Groom); it appears first  fragmented, and then subsequently unfragmented in the English Horn.  The second most important melody used in this piece is “Boogich Bulgar” (a “Bulgar”—celebratory dance tune—attributed to Jack Boogich).  Additionally, three other tunes make appearances—“Heveinu Shalom Aleichem” (We Brought Peace Upon You), “Fun der Khupe” (From the Wedding Canopy), and bits and pieces of “Hava Nagila” (Let us Rejoice) starting in measure 58—along with suggestions of Richard Strauss’ Till Eulenspiegel.

Klezmory was written for Mark Hilt and the Harvard-Westlake Symphony, and was premiered by them in May, 2009.  It is a bit less than nine minutes in duration.

David S. Lefkowitz

26 January, 2009

Los Angeles CA
